subject: Notice orchestration & subprocessor handover map
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta@healthcorps.io>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-17T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Notice orchestration & subprocessor handover map

Hi Marta —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our conversation, I wanted to put a lightweight proposal on timeline and roles for incident notices that involve subprocessors and cross-border handover. This is intended to make sure your legal and forensics teams have a practical playbook we can operate against (not contractual language yet).

High-level proposal (attached: redwood_dpa_incident_clause_proposal_v1.docx):
- Initial triage notice: observable incident status and scope, within 6 hours of detection (internal severity >= P2).
- Customer-facing notification (summary of scope + immediate mitigations): within 24 hours of confirmed data exposure affecting customer assets.
- Detailed impact report and forensic artifacts: delivery window within 7 business days, with rolling updates every 48 hours.
- Subprocessor disclosure & handover: list of affected subprocessors and expected handback timeline within 72 hours; full technical handover (logs, tickets, chain-of-custody) within 10 business days.

Operational asks from HealthCorps to enable the above:
1) Point of contact for legal and forensics (name + escalation phone/email).
2) Format for forensic artifacts you require (we included a suggested checklist in forensic_access_checklist.xlsx).
3) Any contractual hard stop (e.g., 48/72-hour SLA) you need us to bake into the DPA redline vs. what you're comfortable keeping as operational SLOs.

Rachel / Ben / Monica — please flag anything you think is missing before I send to Marta and legal@healthcorps.io.

Thanks,
Ava

Thanks Ava — this is helpful and matches the tone we want. A few clarifying Qs from our side before we loop in internal counsel:

1) For the 6-hour triage notice: do you mean 'detection' by your monitoring, or 'confirmation' after you validate exposure? Our legal team generally expects a notification window that starts on confirmation.
2) For subprocessor handback: what level of PII mapping will you provide in the initial 72-hour disclosure? Full record-level maps can take time; a scoped summary is often fine as long as forensic access is available.
3) Cross-border concerns: our users are largely EU-based — any transfer steps or additional controls we should expect?

Marta
Head of Security Operations | HealthCorps
forensics+sec@healthcorps.io

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-17T12:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Notice orchestration & subprocessor handover map

Ava — quick legal POV before we reply to Marta / legal@healthcorps.io:

- Start of clock: contractually we typically define the notification clock as "confirmed incident affecting Customer Data" (i.e., after internal verification that customer data was accessed/exfiltrated). Operationally we can send an early 'holding' triage email at detection to avoid surprises, but C-level timings should reference "confirmed" to avoid false-positive liabilities.
- 72-hour subprocessor disclosure: we can commit to an initial subprocessor list and high-level role+region within 72 hours. Full technical index (per-record mappings) is best-effort and dependent on customer's scope and search parameters — propose we add "best-effort forensic index within 10 business days" as Ava suggested.
- EU transfers: we should signal that where data resides in EU, we will coordinate data access via EU-hosted forensic resources or provide pseudonymized exports where feasible; we shouldn't promise an automatic cross-border transfer without customer approval.

I'll attach a one-page DPA redline summary for the external counsel once we have alignment.

Rachel Kim
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-17T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Notice orchestration & subprocessor handover map

Ava/Rachel — operational notes from forensics/ops side:

- For the 6-hour detection holding: our SOC automation can open an incident ticket + provide initial telemetry within 4 hours of automated detection. Confirmation normally requires at least a minimal manual review; we should be explicit to customers about detection vs confirmation.
- For initial 72-hour subprocessor disclosure: we can provide a table of affected subprocessors with timestamps and the types of processed data (e.g., logs, model cache, user content). We will not provide full raw logs publicly; we will share them through an authenticated SFTP/secure drive with chain-of-custody notes and an agreed scope.
- For EU customers: propose we offer "onshore forensic pods" — a predefined set of engineers and an EU-hosted SFTP instance to avoid cross-border export. If customer requests raw exports from US-hosted infra, we'll require legal approvals and DPA annex sign-off.

I've updated the forensic checklist (forensic_access_checklist.xlsx) with the access templates and transfer knobs.

Ben Carter
Head of Security Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Notice orchestration & subprocessor handover map

Marta / HealthCorps legal —

Thanks for the clarifying questions. Short answers below; attached is a one-page summary we can hand to your counsel and a suggested operational SLA table.

1) "Detection vs confirmation": we will do an automated holding notice at detection (aiming within 6 hours) and a formal customer confirmation when we have validated that customer data is impacted. The contractual clock should reference "confirmation"; the holding notice is a courtesy to help you stand up internal triage.
2) "PII mapping in 72 hours": initial 72-hour disclosure will include: affected subprocessor names, roles, data categories (e.g., user identifiers, content, metadata), and the provisional containment measures taken. We will commit to a full indexed export or scoped forensic package within 10 business days, subject to mutually agreed scopes and legal controls.
3) "Cross-border/Onshore pods": for EU user data we will default to EU-hosted forensic access. Any transfer of raw data out of EU will require HealthCorps' written consent and the DPA annex procedures (we flagged the clause in the attached DPA proposal).

Next steps:
- Please confirm PoCs for legal + forensics (name + preferred secure channel) and whether you want the contractual 24/72/10bd timings to be binding or operational SLOs.
- If HealthCorps legal wants, Rachel will send a concise DPA redline for deadlining next week.

Attachments: redwood_dpa_incident_clause_proposal_v1.docx; forensic_access_checklist.xlsx

Best,
Ava
